consensus_summary: Consensus treats 'shadow' as polyvalent and context-dependent, with two leading candidates for primary sense (divine protection/refuge under God's wings or shade; NT typological foreshadowing where OT rites are shadow and Christ/heavenly things the substance) plus common alternatives of life's transience and the shadow of death/gloom; no single settled ranking.
book_summary: Shadow is an object or activity shaped like the substance that casts it and that marks the reach and boundary of that substance's covering; the appointed times and holy assemblies are specifically the shadow of Christ's substance, with Shadow of Death as its opposite.
consensus_core_identification: Either (or both) divine protective covering/refuge or incomplete typological foreshadowing of Christ's substance.
book_core_identification: The shaped outline that marks the reach/boundary of a substance's covering, instantiated by the appointed times/holy assemblies as Christ's shadow.
boundary_disagreement: Book unifies protection and typology under a single 'covering-boundary' definition and restricts the positive typological cases chiefly to appointed times/holy assemblies; it reclassifies 'Shadow of Death' as opposite rather than as one ordinary sense of the term.
material_contradiction: None; the central referents (protective covering and feasts-as-shadow-of-Christ) remain intact.
rationale: Minimum cores overlap on the two dominant consensus senses (covering/protection and Col/Heb typology). The book does not replace those referents but supplies a tighter geometric/covering definition, narrows the typological extension to the feasts of Lev 23, and inverts the status of 'shadow of death.' That is boundary refinement, not core contradiction or novelty.
strongest_objection: Some consensus responses already elevate the Col/Heb typological sense to primary, so the book could be read as near-MATCH once wording differences are discounted.
